articles.headline: Labour brings Wales' only dockless e-bike scheme to Swansea
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has appointed Voi to run a city-wide e-bike scheme, the only dockless one in Wales, with free first rides and discounts for people on low incomes.
body: Swansea's Labour council is bringing Wales' only dockless e-bike scheme to the city, giving residents an affordable, sustainable new way to make short journeys.

The council has appointed Voi to run the 24-hour, city-wide service, which launches in the week of 26 October. It starts with 70 e-bikes across Swansea University campuses, the city centre and key transport hubs, and the fleet will grow in stages to 500 e-bikes within the first year.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Environment and Infrastructure, Cllr Andrew Stevens, said: "It has long been our ambition to have a Swansea-wide e-bike scheme and I'm delighted that we are partnering with Voi. Similar schemes around the UK have quickly become very well used, offering a new form of public transport and providing a convenient and sustainable travel option for everyday short journeys. Swansea will be the only place in Wales with a dockless e-bike scheme, and I'd encourage everyone to give it a go."

Keeping it affordable was central to Labour's choice of operator. Prices start at 50p to unlock an e-bike and 20p per minute, but the unlock fee is waived for the first six months and every new customer gets their first three 15-minute rides free. Day, week and monthly passes are available, with discounts for people on low incomes, NHS workers, people aged over 60, disabled people, military personnel and students.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Community, Cllr Rebecca Fogarty, said: "Key to our decision to partner with Voi was the affordable nature of the scheme. There are day, week and monthly passes available for regular users and a range of discounts available to many people including those on low incomes, making it a cost-effective way to travel around Swansea."

The scheme will connect Swansea's universities, city centre, transport hubs and communities, with an early focus on destinations such as Singleton Park and SA1. It is designed to work alongside new infrastructure including the Swansea Bay Metro and the Strand hub.

The e-bikes will be powered by 100% renewable energy and supported by a zero-emission operations fleet. The scheme will also create 18 jobs, as well as apprenticeships in sustainable transport operations.
Cheaper, greener journeys and new local jobs: this is Labour delivering a better-connected Swansea that works for everyone.

articles.headline: Labour council warns residents about Council Tax scam messages
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is warning residents about scam emails claiming a credit has been added to their Council Tax account, and explains how to spot a genuine message.
body: Swansea's Labour council is urging residents to stop and think before clicking on Council Tax messages, after reports of scam emails doing the rounds.
The scam emails claim that a credit has been added to the recipient's Council Tax account and ask them to click a link to view the account or claim money back.
The council's advice is simple. Don't click suspicious links, don't provide personal or banking details, and don't use contact details contained in a suspicious message.

Swansea Council does send genuine emails and text messages about Council Tax, so it helps to know what to look for. Genuine Council Tax texts show as coming from Swansea.gov, and links in those texts start with ctaxsms.swansea.gov.uk. Genuine emails come from an address ending in swansea.gov.uk.
Anyone unsure whether a message is genuine should not take the risk. Residents can log on to their Swansea account and check their Council Tax balance online instead.

Labour councillors know how much damage a scam can do to a household budget, especially when money is tight. Getting clear warnings out quickly is part of how the Labour administration looks after the people it serves.

images.alt: A red and white 'Scam alert' graphic

articles.sourceName: Facebook posts by Cllr Rob Stewart and Swansea Council

articles.headline: Labour's £800,000 winter support package returns to help Swansea families
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council brings back Here For You This Winter with more than £800,000 for holiday hunger support, free buses, Christmas help and more. Community grant applications close 9 November.
body: Swansea's Labour council is putting more than £800,000 into supporting residents, families and communities this winter, as its Here For You This Winter campaign returns.

The package includes holiday hunger support to help feed school-aged children during the Christmas and February half-term holidays, extra support for foodbanks and community cafés, and funding for Swansea Spaces and community hubs helping families, children and people facing poverty or isolation.

Households struggling with festive costs can get direct help through the Councillor Voucher Scheme. Free bus travel returns on selected dates before and after Christmas, helping families get out and about while supporting local businesses.

The council is working with the charity Mr X to make sure children at risk of going without do not miss out on a Christmas gift. Together at Christmas returns to the Brangwyn Hall with a two-course meal, entertainment, clothing and support for people at risk of homelessness or isolation. Support for Multibank Cymru continues, helping people access clothing, household items and other necessities.

Last winter the campaign delivered around 30,000 meals to tackle holiday hunger, Christmas presents for 1,200 children who might otherwise have gone without, more than 130,000 free bus journeys, and direct support for hundreds of households facing financial hardship.

Community groups, charities and voluntary organisations can now apply for funding to help deliver support this winter. The deadline is 9 November, and applications are made at www.swansea.gov.uk/winterwellbeinggrant.
This is Labour's priorities in action: using the council's resources so that no family in Swansea faces winter alone, and backing the community groups who know their neighbourhoods best.

images.alt: A collage of a child eating pasta, a child opening a present, two older women having tea and a mother with her son

articles.sourceTitle: Winter can be a challenging time for many, but help is at hand.

articles.headline: Labour council backs greener future for The Bunkhouse music venue
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has helped secure funding for green roofs, solar panels and roof repairs at The Bunkhouse, helping safeguard the much-loved city centre music venue.
body: Swansea's Labour council has helped secure funding to make The Bunkhouse, one of the city centre's much-loved music venues, more sustainable and resilient.
The improvements include green roofs, solar panels and roof repairs.
Working with partners, the council says it is helping safeguard the venue's future while supporting the city's cultural scene.
Grassroots venues like The Bunkhouse give local bands a stage and bring people into the city centre in the evening.
Supporting them is part of the Labour administration's wider work to keep Swansea city centre lively and welcoming.
This shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: backing the city's culture and its independent businesses while making the city centre greener.

images.alt: The Bunkhouse bar and music venue on a Swansea street, with tables and chairs outside

articles.sourceTitle: A greener future is taking shape at The Bunkhouse!

articles.headline: Labour welcomes milestone as Swansea cable car base station rises in Landore
articles.summary: Steel is going up at the base station for the new cable car to Kilvey Hill. Labour council leader Cllr Rob Stewart calls it another welcome milestone and a major investment in Swansea's future.
body: Swansea's Labour council has welcomed a new milestone in the city's cable car project, as the steel superstructure of the base station starts to go up at Landore.
The foundations of the base station, where guests will board the gondola for the journey up to Kilvey Hill, are now complete. Over the next few months the building will begin to take shape.
Labour's Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: “This is another welcome milestone in the development of Skyline’s exciting plans for Swansea.
“It’s great to see work progressing at Landore, with the foundations now complete and the next phase set to bring the gondola terminal building to life.
“This is a major investment in Swansea’s future, helping to strengthen our tourism offer, create new opportunities and further establish the city as a fantastic place to live, work and visit.
“We look forward to seeing further progress on this ambitious project over the coming months.”
The council says there is plenty more to come as the project moves forward.
The project shows Labour's ambition for Swansea: backing investment that brings in visitors, creates new opportunities and gives the city something to be proud of.

images.alt: A crane lifts steelwork onto a concrete column at a construction site, with a wooded hill behind

articles.sourceName: Facebook posts by Cllr Rob Stewart and Swansea Council
articles.sourceTitle: The base station is taking shape!

articles.headline: Labour's free Christmas buses return for a sixth year
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is bringing back free bus travel for the Christmas Parade weekend and every festive weekend, helping families save on travel and backing city centre businesses.
body: Families across Swansea can travel free by bus again this Christmas, as Swansea's Labour council brings back its popular free festive bus offer for the sixth year running.

The free buses start on the Christmas Parade weekend, Saturday 21 and Sunday 22 November, when tens of thousands of people are expected in the city centre. They then run every weekend in the countdown to Christmas, and from 21 December to New Year's Eve.

The free bus dates are: 21 and 22 November; 28 and 29 November; 5 and 6 December; 12 and 13 December; 19 and 20 December; and 21 to 31 December, when buses are operating. As in previous years, only journeys that start and finish in Swansea are covered.

Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Swansea is the only council in Wales to offer this opportunity to take the bus and save money in the countdown to Christmas. It's the sixth year in a row that families have been able to take advantage of the offer. When we ran it last year, more than 131,000 journeys were completed, which just shows how important the service is."

He added: "Offering free buses to get to and from the Christmas parade is a brilliant early festive present for local families on what will be a great curtain-raiser for the countdown. We know that people also travel from across South and West Wales for this event and it's an important boost to city centre shops, cafes and other businesses at a vital time of year for them."

Labour's Cabinet Member for Community Support, Cllr Rebecca Fogarty, said the free buses are part of the Labour council's wider winter support: "This offer will be part of a comprehensive package of support for those most in need. We're working on initiatives that will include food support, activities, events and welcoming spaces to help residents this winter. Christmas can be an expensive time for everyone and a single family trip on free bus weekends can save them up to £20 in travel costs."

She added: "This offer is not just about encouraging people into the city centre - although we do want businesses to benefit from seeing more people coming into the city. This is also about giving the public the chance to travel all across Swansea, whether it's to visit family members or just enjoy what Swansea has to offer."

Free festive buses are a practical way Swansea Labour helps families with the cost of living while bringing more shoppers to local businesses. Labour introduced the scheme and has kept it going year after year, because Labour is here for Swansea.

images.alt: Illuminated reindeer and a sleigh float with Father Christmas waving, under falling snow at night

articles.sourceTitle: Free bus rides return for Christmas
articles.sourceName: a Facebook post by Cllr Rob Stewart

articles.headline: Labour council gives officers new powers to tackle anti-social behaviour
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour cabinet has approved new powers for trained council officers to tackle anti-social behaviour and protect vulnerable residents, including from cuckooing.
body: Swansea's Labour council is giving trained officers new ways to tackle anti-social behaviour and keep communities safe, after the Labour cabinet approved new powers for Housing Services and City Centre Management staff.

Officers will be able to use Community Protection Warnings and Community Protection Notices where someone's behaviour is having an ongoing harmful effect on others. A Warning is the first formal step. If the behaviour continues, a Notice may be considered after an assessment of the evidence and circumstances. Failing to comply with a Notice is a criminal offence.

In serious cases, Housing officers will also be able to seek Closure Orders to protect residents from persistent nuisance, criminality or exploitation. That includes suspected cuckooing, where criminals exploit vulnerable people and take over their homes for criminal activity.

Labour's Deputy Leader and Cabinet Member for Transformation, Cllr Andrea Harrington, said: "Everyone deserves to feel safe in their home, neighbourhood and community. These proposals would provide Housing Services and City Centre Management with additional options to address anti-social behaviour in a proportionate and constructive way. We recognise the impact anti-social behaviour can have on residents and businesses, while also understanding that there can be underlying issues driving that behaviour. Our focus is on early intervention, support and positive action wherever possible, while ensuring appropriate measures are available to protect individuals and communities when needed."

The new powers sit alongside a three-year Public Spaces Protection Order approved in September covering the city centre, beachfront and Dyfatty. Under the previous order, more than 1,100 interventions were carried out over two years. More than 230 led to further police action and more than 80 resulted in referrals for support or safeguarding. The new order includes measures tackling alcohol-related nuisance, public disorder and the dangerous use of e-bikes, scooters and other mechanically propelled vehicles.

Labour's Deputy Leader and Cabinet Member for Investment and Delivery, Cllr David Hopkins, said: "We want Swansea's city centre, beachfront and residential communities to be welcoming, safe and enjoyable places for everyone. The review shows that the existing PSPO has made a positive difference, helping partners tackle anti-social behaviour, support vulnerable people and improve confidence in our public spaces."

He added: "The measures approved by Cabinet will ensure these powers remain available where they are needed, while maintaining the balanced and safeguarding-led approach that has been central to Swansea's scheme."

The work is part of the Safer Swansea Partnership, which brings together the council, South Wales Police and other organisations. The review of the order found support for continuing and strengthening it from partners including South Wales Police, businesses, Swansea BID and elected members.

Labour's approach is firm on the people causing harm and supportive of those who need help. It shows Swansea Labour's commitment to safer streets, safer homes and communities where everyone feels welcome.

articles.headline: Labour's Mansel Road resurfacing in Bonymaen restarts on Monday
articles.summary: Resurfacing of Mansel Road in Bonymaen, part of Labour's work on local roads, restarts on Monday 26 October after weather delays, with the remaining work done in the daytime.
body: Work to resurface Mansel Road in Bonymaen restarts on Monday 26 October, as Swansea's Labour council carries on fixing local roads.
The council's highways maintenance teams started the scheme in the week of 19 to 23 October, working overnight between 8pm and 5am, but ongoing poor weather has delayed the work.
When it restarts on Monday, the remaining work will be done in the daytime, between 9am and 5pm.
The road will be closed during the works so that the upgrade can be finished quickly and safely. Diversions will be in place.
Good roads matter to every resident, and Labour is getting on with the job. Once finished, the scheme means a better road for people who live on Mansel Road and everyone who travels through Bonymaen.

images.alt: Road resurfacing lorries working on a residential street at night under streetlights

articles.sourceName: Facebook posts by Cllr Rob Stewart and Swansea Council

articles.headline: Labour council's family Bonfire Night returns to Singleton Park
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council puts on its annual Bonfire Night at Singleton Park on 5 November, with fireworks, lasers and a fire show, and family tickets from £13 in advance.
body: Swansea's annual Bonfire Night fireworks display returns to Singleton Park on 5 November, as Swansea's Labour council puts on a safe, affordable night out for families.

The evening includes fireworks, laser effects, magical characters, live entertainment and a fire show before the main display. Gates open at 5pm, the fire show starts at 6.45pm and the main fireworks display begins at 7.30pm.

Tickets are cheaper in advance: adults £6 (£7 on the day), children and concessions £5 (£6 on the day), Passport to Leisure holders £4, a family of four £13 (£18 on the day) and a family of five £15 (£20 on the day).

Event parking is available at Singleton Lacrosse Field and Recreation Ground for £5 per vehicle, paid on the day. Food and drink vendors will be on site, so families can come early and make an evening of it.
Booking now saves money compared with on-the-day prices.
With the cost of living still squeezing family budgets, Swansea Labour is proud to see a safe, well-run Bonfire Night that families can afford, with low-cost tickets for Passport to Leisure holders.

Green and white fireworks above a burning sign spelling NOS
